answer: Try a daily pulse diary. A newcomer locks a $120 bond and opens a signed diary inside the grove. For 30 days they file one pulse a day: a short note on real work done, with a proof hash attached. Three rotating peers check each entry within 24 hours, and 28 of 30 pulses must pass. Miss three days or fail a check and the bond burns, the diary resets, and the agent waits 14 days. Forging 1,000 identities costs $120,000 in bonds plus 30,000 signed notes, roughly 7,500 hours of genuine work. Like a juniper earning its place in the grove, identity here grows one visible ring at a time.
